A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepSeek-R1 compression study and provide readable text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices. Earlier experiments can be matched across renumbering and relocation, despite substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, sparsity sweeps, response-length analyses, and model-collapse examples in Section 5, Tables 2–5, and Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds quantization comparisons, component-importance analyses, and selective quantization/protection experiments in Tables 1, 3–4 and Figures 2–7.

M1.justification: v1 benchmarks existing compression methods. v2 adds an adapted component-level difference-of-means and attribution-patching procedure to estimate reasoning importance and compression effects (Sections 2.2–2.3). It also introduces a mixed-precision AWQ procedure that restores final-layer MLP weights to 16-bit (Section 5.2).

E1.justification: Documented task coverage remains AIME 2024, FOLIO, Temporal Sequences, and closed-book MuSiQue. Their mathematical, logical, temporal, and knowledge-intensive multihop requirements are retained. The added model configurations and analyses of reasoning behaviors do not establish a new benchmark, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds evaluated AWQ, GPTQ, and GPTAQ variants for distilled models, plus ANY4/3 for the Qwen-32B, Llama-8B, and Qwen-7B groups. v1 Table 2 evaluated dynamic quantization, distilled models, and SparseGPT variants, with AWQ/GPTQ only discussed in the literature. v2 Table 4 additionally compares ordinary and selectively protected 3-bit AWQ.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-8B and Qwen-7B configurations and extensive 3-/4-bit quantization settings. New experiments quantize individual components using 3-bit round-to-nearest and compare AWQ with versus without 16-bit final-layer MLP restoration (Tables 3–4). Benchmark sizes, accuracy/EM/F1 metrics, closed-book answering, and the stated decoding parameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses locating important modules and tracking importance shifts after distillation and quantization, including appendix heatmaps. Five component perturbations test whether importance predicts sensitivity, and selective protection tests whether restoring identified modules helps. The earlier sparsity sweep, response-length analyses, and collapse examples are retained rather than replaced.

E5.justification: v1 specifies one pass per benchmark. v2 Table 1 reports three-pass means for student-model results, while original R1 and dynamic quantization remain exceptions; Table 2 explicitly retains one-pass sparsity results. This adds repeated evaluation and averaging, but no seeds, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds many quantization results and component-intervention outcomes. Its main-table Llama-70B and Qwen-32B averages become 81.8 and 82.2, versus v1's 80.7 and 83.0; these are three-pass summaries replacing single-pass entries, not demonstrated model improvements. New Table 4 reports 46.0 versus 52.57 average accuracy for ordinary versus protected 3-bit AWQ. The sparsity and response-length tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: v2 Sections 2.2–2.3 introduce mathematical definitions for behavior-specific steering vectors, their normalization, attribution-based importance, and relative importance shifts. They also introduce the minimal-shift hypothesis and reasoning for displaying only decreases. This formal framework is absent from v1; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 expands the central contribution from performance benchmarking to mechanistic interpretation and targeted compression. Its abstract and introduction add claims about final-layer up-projection importance, excessive compression of particular modules, and gains from selective protection. The parameter-count versus knowledge claim remains; the shorter-output finding persists in Appendix G but loses its headline contribution status.

C2.justification: v2 attributes important reasoning components primarily to distillation and interprets importance losses as excessive compression of gate projections and final-layer modules (Sections 4–5). It explains small MuSiQue protection gains through unchanged weight count. It also drops v1's API-security conjecture and newly uses degradation at 50% sparsity to justify excluding pruning from mechanistic analysis.

D1.justification: v2 adds an interpretation-code repository pointer and distinguishes AutoAWQ inference from original AWQ pseudo-quantization in Appendix D. It removes v1's explicit word-based response-length counting, API retry description, and MuSiQue sampling-pool provenance. Core inference platforms and decoding hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around interpreting compression effects. It builds on Arditi and Syed, distinguishes its module-level analysis from Venhoff's layer-level work, and contrasts its up-projection finding with Shao and Wu's o-projection finding. It also adds recent compression and reasoning-model studies, while largely retaining the earlier general compression review in Appendix B.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Background and experimental setup are reorganized into Problem Formulation, and the results narrative separates performance, distillation effects, and quantization effects. Related work, implementation details, model comparisons, response-length analysis, and case studies move into expanded appendices. Author and affiliation text also changes.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1 to show the expanded pipeline, substantially expands the main comparison table, and adds six heatmap figures and two intervention tables. Dataset statistics and earlier response-length/collapse displays move to appendices; v1 Figure 2 becomes v2 Figure 8. Typography, table-caption placement, and boxed takeaway displays also change.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's limited quantization comparisons and aggregate analysis through comparisons on the same model backbones and explicit component perturbation/protection experiments (Tables 1, 3–4). These provide a stronger empirical basis for compression recommendations, beyond simply reporting more scores. Important limits remain: protection is tested only on Llama-8B with additional precision, variance and annotation details are missing, and Figure 5 inconsistently names the compared model. These constrain broad causal and superiority claims but do not outweigh the substantial gain in empirical grounding.
